concept.name: ETL vs ELT Pipelines

relationships.description: Connects ETL vs ELT Pipelines to data warehousing lakehouse in the broader engineering catalog.

spark.summary: ETL transforms raw data on dedicated compute servers before loading it into a target warehouse, whereas ELT loads raw data directly into scalable cloud storage and transforms it in-place using warehouse SQL/compute.
spark.keyTakeaway: Modern cloud data platforms favor ELT for schema agility and raw-history replayability, reserving pre-load ETL for strict PII redaction, high-frequency stream aggregation, and regulatory compliance.

concept.whyItMatters: Choosing between ETL and ELT dictates your data platform's cost structure, schema evolution speed, and compliance posture. Traditional ETL (Informatica, Talend, Spark pre-load jobs) protected expensive, compute-constrained on-premise databases (Oracle, Teradata) by cleaning data before ingestion—but any change in business logic meant re-running upstream pipelines from source systems. Modern cloud warehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks) separate storage (~$20–$23/TB/month) from elastic compute, making ELT (Fivetran/Airbyte + dbt) the default: land raw JSON/Parquet immediately, then transform with version-controlled SQL.
whenToUse: Use ELT when landing data into elastic cloud warehouses or lakehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Iceberg) where analytical requirements evolve weekly.
Use ELT when data scientists and analysts need access to raw, untransformed event payloads to backfill new metrics without re-extracting from OLTP databases.
Use ETL when strict regulatory rules (GDPR, HIPAA, PCI-DSS) forbid raw PII, PANs, or unmasked health records from ever touching the destination data lake.
whenNotToUse: Avoid pure ELT for raw IoT telemetry emitting 500k+ events/sec of noisy sensor readings where pre-filtering/downsampling (ETL) cuts warehouse ingestion and storage bills by 80%.
Avoid heavyweight ETL clusters for simple SaaS-to-warehouse replication (Salesforce, Stripe, HubSpot) where managed ELT connectors + dbt models deploy in hours.
Avoid ELT when the target database is a legacy OLTP or constrained on-prem appliance that cannot absorb large `MERGE` or `JOIN` workloads without starving transactional queries.
keyPoints: Order of operations: ETL runs Extract -> Transform -> Load (curated schema first); ELT runs Extract -> Load -> Transform (raw schema first, curated models later).
Compute engine: ETL relies on external transformation engines (Apache Spark, Flink, Informatica); ELT pushes transformations down into the target MPP engine (Snowflake SQL, BigQuery, Trino).
Replayability: ELT preserves raw immutable staging tables (`bronze` layer), allowing engineers to fix a buggy SQL join and re-materialize `silver`/`gold` tables without touching upstream APIs.
PII & Governance: ETL can tokenize or drop sensitive columns in flight before persistence; ELT requires column-level masking, tokenization UDFs, or a pre-load redaction proxy.
Medallion architecture: Modern lakehouses blend both—lightweight ETL/CDC (Debezium + Kafka) lands clean Avro/Parquet into Bronze, then dbt/Spark ELT builds Silver and Gold.

examples.title: E-Commerce Analytics Migration from Spark ETL to Snowflake + dbt ELT
examples.scenario: A retail platform ran nightly PySpark ETL jobs on EMR to join PostgreSQL orders with Stripe payouts before loading Redshift. Adding a single attribution column took 4 days of pipeline rewrites and backfills.
examples.outcome: Switching to Airbyte/Debezium CDC into Snowflake raw tables (`bronze`) plus dbt SQL models (`silver`/`gold`) cut pipeline lead time from 4 days to 2 hours and reduced EMR idle compute spend by 62%.

examples.title: Healthcare Claims Ingestion with Pre-Load PII ETL
examples.scenario: A health-tech analytics team needed to ingest HL7/FHIR claims into BigQuery for cohort analysis, but HIPAA compliance barred storing unencrypted SSNs and patient names in the analytical warehouse.
examples.outcome: They deployed a stateless Apache Beam (Dataflow) ETL stage before BigQuery that deterministically hashes SSNs with a Cloud KMS-backed HMAC key and strips free-text notes, achieving HIPAA compliance while still running downstream dbt ELT for clinical metrics.

tradeOffs.pro: ELT lands raw data in minutes; analysts write SQL transformations on demand without waiting for data engineering sprints.
tradeOffs.con: Raw landing zones can quickly devolve into an undocumented 'data swamp' without strict dbt testing, ownership, and catalog governance.

tradeOffs.pro: ETL drops unused columns and aggregates noisy logs before load, minimizing destination storage and egress.
tradeOffs.con: ELT duplicates data across Bronze/Silver/Gold layers and can incur runaway warehouse credit bills if unoptimized `dbt run` models scan full multi-terabyte tables.

tradeOffs.pro: ETL enforces tokenization, masking, and row filtering in transit before sensitive data is written to analytical storage.
tradeOffs.con: ELT stores raw payloads at rest first, expanding the blast radius of a warehouse permission misconfiguration.

failureModes.name: Runaway Warehouse Compute in ELT
failureModes.description: A `dbt run` schedule executes full-table refreshes every 15 minutes on a 10 TB event table instead of incremental `MERGE` models, burning thousands of dollars in Snowflake/BigQuery slots.
failureModes.mitigation: Use incremental materializations partitioned by `event_date`, enforce cluster keys, and set warehouse resource monitors with hard credit caps.

failureModes.name: Upstream Schema Drift Breaking Rigid ETL
failureModes.description: An upstream microservice renames or adds a JSON field; a brittle ETL Spark job with a hardcoded Avro/SQL schema fails at 03:00 AM, halting all downstream dashboards.
failureModes.mitigation: In ELT, land semi-structured payloads in `VARIANT`/`JSON` columns, use schema-registry compatibility checks (`BACKWARD`), and alert on unexpected null rates.

failureModes.name: PII Leakage into Raw ELT Staging
failureModes.description: A developer enables 'sync all columns' on a Fivetran/Debezium connector, inadvertently replicating `password_hash`, `ssn`, or `credit_card_token` into an analyst-accessible raw schema.
failureModes.mitigation: Maintain explicit column allowlists at the ingestion connector and apply automated PII scanners (e.g., BigQuery DLP, Snowflake Horizon) on landing schemas.

failureModes.name: Silent Late-Arriving Data Skew
failureModes.description: Mobile clients buffer offline events for 48 hours; an incremental ETL/ELT job filtering only `WHERE created_at >= yesterday` permanently misses late events.
failureModes.mitigation: Use a rolling lookback window (e.g., `event_ts >= current_date - 3 days`) keyed on ingestion timestamp (`_loaded_at`) during incremental merges.

commonMistakes: Treating ELT as an excuse to skip data modeling—querying raw JSON blobs directly from BI tools instead of building tested Silver/Gold tables.
Running heavy row-by-row Python UDFs inside a SQL warehouse during ELT instead of using native vectorized SQL or external Spark.
Failing to deduplicate CDC/webhook retries (`at-least-once` ingestion), which inflates revenue metrics by 2x during upstream hiccups.
Putting business logic in both the ingestion ETL script AND downstream dbt SQL, creating two conflicting sources of truth.
Ignoring GDPR 'Right to be Forgotten' delete propagation across immutable Bronze Parquet/Iceberg snapshots.

sections.content:
## The idea

Every analytical pipeline performs three verbs: **Extract** bytes from operational sources (Postgres, Kafka, SaaS APIs), **Transform** them (deduplicate, cast types, mask PII, join dimensions), and **Load** them into an analytical store. The sole architectural distinction between ETL and ELT is **where and when Transform runs**.

In **ETL**, transformation happens *in flight* on a dedicated external cluster (Spark, Informatica, AWS Glue) before the target database ever sees a row. In **ELT**, raw data is loaded *immediately* into a cloud warehouse or lakehouse (Snowflake, BigQuery, Databricks), and transformations execute *in place* via distributed SQL or DataFrame engines (dbt, Spark SQL).

## Concrete walkthrough

Trace a 50-million-row daily order stream from PostgreSQL to a BI dashboard under **hybrid ELT (Medallion)**:

1. **Extract & Load (Debezium + Kafka -> Iceberg Bronze)**: Debezium reads Postgres WAL logical replication slots and emits change events to Kafka. A lightweight sink writes raw Parquet files into an Apache Iceberg `bronze.orders_raw` table partitioned by `_ingested_date` with zero business joins.
2. **In-Place Transform 1 (dbt Silver)**: Every 15 minutes, a `dbt` incremental model reads new Bronze rows using `_ingested_ts > max(target._ingested_ts)`, deduplicates by `(order_id, updated_at DESC)`, casts currency cents to `DECIMAL(12,2)`, and writes `silver.orders_clean`.
3. **In-Place Transform 2 (dbt Gold)**: A downstream `dbt` model joins `silver.orders_clean` with `silver.customers` and `silver.fx_rates` to materialize `gold.daily_revenue_by_region`, running `not_null` and `unique` schema tests before Looker/Tableau queries it.

sections.eyebrow: 03 / Why cloud economics flipped ETL to ELT
sections.content:
## Why cloud economics flipped ETL to ELT

Two hardware shifts made ELT dominant over the last decade:

1. **Decoupled Storage & Compute**: In legacy appliances, disk and CPU scaled together—storing 50 TB of raw JSON meant buying expensive database nodes. On S3/GCS + Snowflake/BigQuery, storing 50 TB of compressed Parquet costs ~$1,150/month, while compute spins up only during query execution.
2. **MPP Vectorized Execution**: Modern columnar engines execute vectorized SIMD scans over Parquet/micro-partitions at gigabytes per second per node. Pushing `JOIN` and `GROUP BY` into the warehouse avoids serializing terabytes out over the network to an external ETL cluster and back.

## ETL vs. ELT architectural comparison

| Dimension | Classic ETL | Modern ELT | Hybrid (Streaming ETL + Batch ELT) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Transform Location** | External cluster (Spark, Glue, Informatica) | Target warehouse (Snowflake, BigQuery, Trino) | Flink/Beam in-flight + dbt in-warehouse |
| **Raw History Preserved** | Usually discarded post-load | Yes (Bronze / raw schema) | Yes (masked Bronze layer) |
| **PII Redaction** | Pre-storage (strictest) | Post-load masking / dynamic views | Pre-storage tokenization + warehouse RBAC |
| **Schema Flexibility** | Schema-on-write (rigid) | Schema-on-read -> curated marts | Contracted Avro/Protobuf + flexible marts |
| **Typical Latency** | Batch (hourly/nightly) | Micro-batch (5–60 min) | Sub-second alerts + 15-min BI marts |
| **Primary Tooling** | Spark, NiFi, Talend, SSIS | Fivetran, Airbyte, dbt, SQLMesh | Kafka, Debezium, Flink, Iceberg, dbt |

## Failure modes

- **Unbounded Backfill Costs**: Re-running a full-refresh `dbt` DAG over 5 years of unpartitioned event logs can spike monthly warehouse spend by 5x. Always partition by event timestamp and test backfills on a 7-day slice first.
- **GDPR Deletion Gaps**: Deleting a user from Postgres does not erase their historical snapshots in Bronze Iceberg/S3 files. Implement periodic Iceberg `DELETE` + `rewrite_data_files` compaction or crypto-shredding (per-user KMS keys).
- **Circular Model Dependencies**: Without DAG linting, analysts build `gold_a -> silver_b -> gold_a` cycles or reference Bronze directly from dashboards, bypassing quality checks.

sections.eyebrow: 06 / Production patterns: Data contracts and testing
sections.content:
## Production patterns: Data contracts and testing

To prevent ELT from turning into an unmaintainable tangle of SQL views, enforce software engineering rigor on transformations:

- **Data Contracts**: Validate producer schemas at the Kafka/API boundary using Protobuf or JSON Schema with backward compatibility.
- **Staging -> Intermediate -> Marts**: Enforce strict layering via `dbt` directory rules so BI tools only query `gold` mart tables.
- **Automated Quality Gates**: Run `not_null`, `unique`, `accepted_values`, and freshness SLAs (`warn_after: 30m`, `error_after: 2h`) in CI/CD before merging any SQL model change.

## Practical checklist

- [ ] Classify data sensitivity first: redact or tokenize regulated PII (SSN, PAN, PHI) *before* persistence if compliance requires it.
- [ ] Land raw data in an immutable, append-only `bronze` layer with `_ingested_at` and `_source_system` metadata columns.
- [ ] Configure incremental `MERGE` models with a 2–3 day lookback window to capture late-arriving mobile/webhook events.
- [ ] Partition large tables (>100 GB) by date and cluster by high-cardinality filter keys (`tenant_id`, `user_id`).
- [ ] Add automated `dbt` schema tests (`unique`, `not_null`, referential integrity) and freshness monitors on every Gold table.
- [ ] Set hard compute quotas and auto-suspend timers on transformation warehouses to prevent runaway SQL bills.

interviewProblems.title: ETL vs ELT Pipelines
interviewProblems.scenarioPrompt: Design a production system that depends on ETL vs ELT Pipelines. What invariants, failure modes, and observability do you require?
interviewProblems.sampleDefense: Start from invariants, choose the pattern that preserves them, and add metrics for the known failure modes.
commonPitfalls: Optimizing throughput before defining correctness boundaries.

steps.title: 1. Normal Request Ingress
steps.explanation: ETL transforms raw data on dedicated compute servers before loading it into a target warehouse, whereas ELT loads raw data directly into scalable cloud storage and transforms it in-place using warehouse SQL/compute.

steps.title: 2. Core Execution & State Lookup
steps.explanation: Raw Lakehouse (Bronze) applies the primary invariant and coordinates with Curated Models (Silver/Gold).

steps.title: 3. Scale Spike / Failure Injection
steps.explanation: Under a 10x burst, Curated Models (Silver/Gold) experiences contention and tail-latency amplification.

steps.title: 4. Mitigation & Steady Recovery
steps.explanation: Use incremental materializations partitioned by `event_date`, enforce cluster keys, and set warehouse resource monitors with hard credit caps.

tipsAndTricks: Core mental model: Modern cloud data platforms favor ELT for schema agility and raw-history replayability, reserving pre-load ETL for strict PII redaction, high-frequency stream aggregation, and regulatory compliance.
Avoid trap: Treating ELT as an excuse to skip data modeling—querying raw JSON blobs directly from BI tools instead of building tested Silver/Gold tables.
Avoid trap: Running heavy row-by-row Python UDFs inside a SQL warehouse during ELT instead of using native vectorized SQL or external Spark.
When to reach for it: Use ELT when landing data into elastic cloud warehouses or lakehouses (Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, Iceberg) where analytical requirements evolve weekly.
When to reach for it: Use ELT when data scientists and analysts need access to raw, untransformed event payloads to backfill new metrics without re-extracting from OLTP databases.

putItTogether.title: Putting Etl Vs Elt Together
putItTogether.summary: Modern cloud data platforms favor ELT for schema agility and raw-history replayability, reserving pre-load ETL for strict PII redaction, high-frequency stream aggregation, and regulatory compliance.
steps: Establish baseline invariants for Etl Vs Elt before scaling.
Isolate hot paths with caching, backpressure, or partitioning.
Verify failure modes with synthetic load & chaos checks.
putItTogether.outcome: Switching to Airbyte/Debezium CDC into Snowflake raw tables (`bronze`) plus dbt SQL models (`silver`/`gold`) cut pipeline lead time from 4 days to 2 hours and reduced EMR idle compute spend by 62%.
